analysis:
In September 2013 the Delhi Chief Minister released the Delhi Statistical Handbook, which put the capital's per capita income at Rs 2,01,083 for 2012-13 against a national average of about Rs 61,564, and it was widely reported as the highest in the country. A 2011 release of the same handbook made a similar claim for 2009-10.

government/RBI state-wise (NSDP per capita) data for 2012-13 place Goa at about Rs 2,34,354, higher than Delhi's figure, while Delhi remained above other major states and above Sikkim.

The claim as stated ('highest in the country') is therefore not accurate if Goa is counted; Delhi's income was at the top among the large states/UTs but not the highest nationally. The claim is graded misleading rather than false because it was true relative to most states and was the official position of the Delhi government's own statistics office.
notes: The comparison relies on RBI/NSDP per-capita data accessed via a secondary compilation; the exact RBI table was not opened directly. Delhi government figures (Rs 2,01,083) and RBI series (Rs 2,05,568) differ slightly. No verbatim transcript of the Chief Minister's remarks was located.
